body:
Related #40529

## Problem

`vim.filetype.match()` needs a cheap way to recognize directory buffers without doing filesystem stat work. 

## Solution

Make full buffer names for directories end in a trailing slash. Now, directory buffers go through the normal filetype path.

Note that there are a few reamifications for this change: session and ShaDa buffer-list restore behavior must be compatible, so those + corresponding tests must be updated too (see the failing ci in the first commit).

comment_data.body: should probably go before `normalize_path` , just in case...
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -3255,6 +3255,9 @@ function M.match(args)
 
   if name then
     name = normalize_path(name)
+    if name:sub(-1) == '/' then
+      return 'directory'

comment_data.body: still working on a better way to do with restored session directory paths
don't think we want modelines for directories..
does the docstring need an update?
this is a lot of code, and not easy to follow. also surprising that `os_isdir` is called twice, surely the first result can be used later?
updated.
removed

Made it one call.

The rest is the trailing-slash handling, which we can't really avoid: fix_fname resolves the final component when the path ends in a slash, so for `:e link/` where link is a symlinked dir it turns link into the target and loses the spelling.

basically we strip the slash -> expand -> add back, but only when it's a dir. Note that do_ecmd runs `fix_fname` on ffname 
before this point in the code so only `sfname` has the original spelling

i enumerated every case of `:e <dir>` and `:e <file>`, with symlinked dirs/files and fake/non-existing dirs and files and made sure that the behavior matches.

Added some comments to clarify.
